newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares rebound after three days of fall.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares rebound after three days of fall.

text.p: Hungarian share prices rebounded on Wednesday more than regaining Tuesday's losses as a positive mood spread among brokers, traders said.
After three days of decline the BUX index closed at 3,572.75 points, up 49.54.

"The trend reversed due to brokers' optimism," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. "It seems that demand has increased again for Hungarian stocks although the intensity is not that high as it has been before."
The optimism is a result of a general opinion shared by many that Hungarian share prices would stabilise at or slightly above current levels after profit-taking earlier this week.
More than half of company results have already been published so the focus has shifted on to those companies which are still ahead of releasing their earnings report, she said.
MOL ended at 1,620 forints, up 20, while OTP advanced 55 forints to 2,735. Both remained slightly short of the day's peaks.
Brewery Soproni surged almost 15 percent or 300 forints to finish at 2,400 in active trade with mainly speculators seen on the buying side after the release of January-September results.
Meat food processor Pick continued to rise after the release of its results earlier this week. It firmed 200 forints to finish at to 7,400.
